scenes.narration: An array is a list of items stored in adjacent slots.
An array is like a row of numbered mailboxes where each box holds a single piece of mail.

The key rule is that every slot has an index, and indexes start at 0, so the computer can jump straight to any index without looking at the others. The price is that inserting in the middle shifts every later item over.
We initialize the array with values 10, 20, 30, and 40. Array is now [10, 20, 30, 40].
The index lets us jump straight to 30 at index 2 without looking at any other item. Array is now [10, 20, 30, 40].
Insert 15 at index 1; later items shift right. Array is now [10, 15, 20, 30, 40].
Arrays are used in real life to store pixel colors in an image or a list of high scores in a game.
Takeaways: slot numbers start at 0, reading any slot is a single quick step, and inserting in the middle makes later items shift. Array is [10, 15, 20, 30, 40].
